lessons.title: Introduction to Acids
lessons.summary: What makes a substance an acid, and how we recognize one.

blocks.text: An acid is a substance that releases H+ ions when dissolved in water. Common examples include HCl, H2SO4, and CH3COOH (acetic acid, found in vinegar).

items: React with metals to release H2 gas

blocks.caption: Common acids and where they're found

blocks.text: Never taste a substance in the lab to test if it's an acid — always use litmus paper or a pH meter instead.

blocks.title: Reaction of an acid with a metal
blocks.text:
Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2

When zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, hydrogen gas is released — you can test for it with a lit splint, which produces a characteristic 'pop' sound.

lessons.title: The pH Scale
lessons.summary: Measuring how acidic or basic a solution is, from 0 to 14.

blocks.text: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14, and tells you how acidic or basic a solution is.

blocks.title: Calculating pH
blocks.text:
If [H+] = 1 x 10^-3 moldm3, then:
pH = -log10(1 x 10^-3) = 3

This solution is strongly acidic.
A change of 1 on the pH scale means a 10x change in acidity — pH 4 is ten times more acidic than pH 5.

lessons.title: Mean, Median and Mode
lessons.summary: The three most common ways to describe the 'center' of a data set.

rows: The average — add all values, divide by how many there are
The middle value when data is arranged in order
The value that appears most often

blocks.title: Finding the median
blocks.text:
Data: 3, 7, 9, 12, 15

Arranged in order, the middle value (3rd of 5) is 9.
So the median is 9.
If there's an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle numbers.
